newsitem.title: USA: Conn. atty general seeks motorcycle, funeral laws.
newsitem.headline: Conn. atty general seeks motorcycle, funeral laws.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal on Tuesday urged state legislators to extend the state's "lemon law" to motorcycles, and to increase protections for buyers of pre-paid funeral contracts.
The measures were among several consumer protection bills Blumenthal asked lawmakers to consider.
Blumenthal said in a statement that more than 44,000 motorcycle owners in Connecticut were "vulnerable to widespread abuse" because of a 1996 state supreme court ruling.
The ruling said motorcycles were not passenger vehicles and were therefore not covered under the state's existing "lemon law."
Blumenthal also proposed greater protections against pre-paid funeral fraud for consumers, requiring disclosures that would encourage consumers to monitor more closely how their money was handled.
He said pre-paid funeral contracts were a growing business representing about $150 million of consumers' money invested in escrow accounts.

The bill would require each funeral service contract to provide a summary of the consumer's rights under Connecticut law, the name of the escrow agent, and the agent's business address and telephone number.
"Unfortunately, my office has had to pursue court action to help families whose pre-paid funeral funds were absconded with by a funeral home director," said Blumenthal.
"This brand of fraud is especially reprehensible because it often victimizes senior citizens and causes their families added grief and financial burden at a time when they are most vulnerable."
